t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup: a warm limestone sheet inset within a deep navy frame. Top left: a small sans eyebrow and a large light-weight sans headline. Left: a three-column table of <CONTENT> with steel-blue row numbers, monospace cells and hairline rules. Right: a large isometric technical line drawing of a polypropylene water skid on a base plate, uniform dark navy hairline strokes, no shading, no hatching, with four tiny leader-line labels at check points. Square corners, flat, calm and precise.
signature_idea: The site checks table sits beside a catalogue line drawing of the skid, with labels marking where each check happens.
strengths: clean line drawing on limestone is very close to the brand's drawing language
table plus drawing pairs evidence with equipment
light headline, mono cells and steel-blue numbers are on-system
lots of calm space; easy to build as a split section
weaknesses: drawing labels do not match the table rows; only four loose points with no numbers
skid shows a metal-looking tank, control box and stainless-style manifold rather than clearly PP
invented specifics (DVS 2207, USP Class VI, ozone) read as real claims
thick navy frame around the sheet adds a heavy border
table text is small and cramped in narrow columns
brand_fit_why: Limestone sheet, navy linework, light headline, mono cells and steel-blue numbers fit well, but labels are unlinked to rows and the equipment drifts off-offer.
